_comment: The schedule. `enabled` here is the whole in-app scheduler; each entry under `jobs` is one job's interval and settings. ⚠ Leaving a job OUT of this file is NOT off: a job with no entry inherits the defaults, which are enabled and daily (lib/cron/rules.mjs → JOB_DEFAULTS). A job that must not run says so in its own registry entry (`enabledByDefault: false`) — the community module's `community-prune` is the shipped example, and it deletes members' correspondence, so it arrives off. To turn such a job on, add it here with "enabled": true. Only jobs this app actually has may be named: a module's job exists once the module is installed, and `node run.mjs cron --list` is what says which those are. ⚠ `ops-watchdog` is the one job here that MAILS, and its two halves belong together: its registry entry says `enabledByDefault: false` so that DELETING the entry below cannot start it by inheritance, and the entry below is the decision to run it — set "enabled": false there to stop the operator mail. Its 360 minutes are not a preference either: its send key is nailed to the UTC day while due-ness counts from the last FINISH, so a daily interval eventually drifts past midnight and skips a day in silence.
